Question
========
What does SIMD allow?


Answerlist
----------
* Multiple instructions on one data
* One instruction on multiple data element
* Different instructions on different cores
* Parallelism accross threads

Solution
========
SIMD stands for Single Instruction Multiple Data: one instruction is applied simultaneously to every element of a vector register.

Answerlist
----------
* 0. That would be MISD, which has no practical implementation.
* 1. This is the definition of Single Instruction Multiple Data.
* 0. That is MIMD, i.e. multi-core or multi-threading.
* 0. Thread level parallelism is MIMD, not SIMD.
